# Helios — System Architecture Document **Version:** 3.2.0 **Status:** Approved **Last Updated:** 2026-09-22 **Owners:** Platform Engineering, Core Services **Classification:** Internal --- ## 1. Overview Helios is a multi-tenant SaaS platform for **real-time logistics orchestration**. Customers (freight brokers, 3PLs, and enterprise shippers) use Helios to ingest shipment telemetry, run route optimization, and expose a unified tracking API to their own downstream consumers. The platform serves roughly **18,000 tenants**, processes **~240k telemetry events/second** at peak, and maintains a **99.95% availability SLO** on the read path. ### 1.1 Design Goals | Goal | Description | Priority | |------|-------------|----------| | Tenant isolation | No tenant can observe or degrade another's workload | P0 | | Read-path availability | Tracking API stays up even during write-path degradation | P0 | | Elastic ingest | Absorb 5× burst without backpressure to customers | P1 | | Sub-second freshness | p95 telemetry-to-queryable under 800ms | P1 | | Cost predictability | Per-tenant unit economics traceable to infrastructure | P2 | ### 1.2 Non-Goals - Helios does **not** provide a transportation management system (TMS). It integrates with existing TMS vendors. - Helios does **not** guarantee ordered delivery across distinct shipment IDs — only within a single shipment's event stream. - Offline/edge-device operation is explicitly out of scope for 3.x. --- ## 2. System Context ```mermaid graph TB subgraph External["External Actors"] Carrier["Carrier Telematics
(GPS / ELD devices)"] TMS["Customer TMS
(SAP TM, Oracle OTM)"] Ops["Ops Dashboard Users"] Downstream["Downstream Consumers
(customer webhooks)"] end subgraph Helios["Helios Platform"] Edge["Edge Gateway"] Ingest["Ingest Pipeline"] Core["Core Services"] Query["Query & API Layer"] Notify["Notification Fabric"] end subgraph Infra["Managed Infrastructure"] Kafka[("Event Bus
Kafka")] PG[("PostgreSQL
Tenant Metadata")] TS[("TimescaleDB
Telemetry")] Redis[("Redis
Hot Cache")] S3[("Object Store
Cold Archive")] end Carrier -->|MQTT / HTTPS| Edge TMS -->|REST / EDI| Edge Edge --> Ingest Ingest --> Kafka Kafka --> Core Core --> PG Core --> TS Core --> Kafka Query --> Redis Query --> TS Query --> PG Ops -->|HTTPS| Query Downstream <-->|Webhook| Notify Kafka --> Notify TS -.->|nightly tiering| S3 style Helios fill:#2d3748,stroke:#4a5568,color:#fff style Infra fill:#1a365d,stroke:#2c5282,color:#fff style External fill:#44337a,stroke:#553c9a,color:#fff ``` --- ## 3. Component Architecture ### 3.1 Edge Gateway The Edge Gateway terminates all inbound customer traffic. It runs as a fleet of stateless Envoy-fronted Go services across three regions. **Responsibilities:** 1. TLS termination and mTLS validation for telematics devices 2. Tenant resolution from API key, JWT claim, or device certificate SAN 3. Rate limiting (token bucket, per-tenant, backed by Redis) 4. Schema validation and protocol normalization (MQTT → internal protobuf) 5. Request tagging with `trace_id`, `tenant_id`, and `ingest_partition_key` **Key configuration:** ```yaml edge_gateway: listeners: - name: telematics-mqtt port: 8883 protocol: mqtt-tls max_connections: 250000 idle_timeout: 300s - name: public-rest port: 443 protocol: http2 max_concurrent_streams: 1024 rate_limits: default_tier: requests_per_second: 500 burst: 2000 enterprise_tier: requests_per_second: 10000 burst: 40000 tenant_resolution: strategies: [device_cert_san, jwt_claim, api_key] cache_ttl: 60s fail_mode: closed # reject on resolution failure ``` > **Note:** `fail_mode: closed` is deliberate. An unresolvable tenant means we cannot enforce isolation or billing, so we reject rather than route to a default tenant. ### 3.2 Ingest Pipeline The ingest pipeline is a Flink job graph consuming from the Edge Gateway's Kafka topics. | Stage | Operator | Parallelism | Backpressure Strategy | |-------|----------|-------------|----------------------| | Deserialize | `ProtoDecode` | 96 | Drop + DLQ after 3 failures | | Deduplicate | `KeyedDedupe` | 96 | RocksDB state, 10-min window | | Enrich | `GeofenceJoin` | 48 | Async I/O, 2s timeout | | Score | `ETAPredictor` | 48 | Bounded queue, depth 512 | | Sink | `TimescaleSink` | 32 | Batched upsert, 5k rows | **Deduplication key:** `(tenant_id, shipment_id, device_ts_bucket_1s)` Devices commonly retransmit on flaky cellular links; observed duplicate rate is **3.1%** at p50 and spikes to **19%** during regional network events. ### 3.3 Core Services | Service | Language | Datastore | SLO | On-call rotation | |---------|----------|-----------|-----|------------------| | `shipment-svc` | Go | PostgreSQL | 99.95% | core-services | | `route-optimizer` | Rust | Redis + S3 | 99.9% | optimization | | `geofence-svc` | Go | PostGIS | 99.9% | core-services | | `tenant-svc` | Java | PostgreSQL | 99.99% | platform | | `billing-meter` | Go | Kafka + PG | 99.5% | platform | | `notify-fabric` | Elixir | Redis | 99.9% | integrations | --- ## 4. Data Flow: Shipment Status Update The following sequence covers the highest-volume path in the system — a telematics ping that crosses a geofence and triggers a customer webhook. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant D as Telematics Device participant E as Edge Gateway participant K as Kafka participant F as Flink Ingest participant G as geofence-svc participant T as TimescaleDB participant S as shipment-svc participant N as notify-fabric participant C as Customer Webhook D->>E: MQTT PUBLISH (position, mTLS) E->>E: Resolve tenant from cert SAN E->>E: Rate limit check (Redis token bucket) alt Rate limit exceeded E-->>D: PUBACK with throttle hint Note over E: Event dropped, metric emitted else Within limit E->>K: produce → telemetry.raw (key=shipment_id) K->>F: consume batch F->>F: Deduplicate (10-min RocksDB window) F->>G: Async geofence lookup (2s timeout) alt Geofence service degraded G--xF: timeout F->>F: Mark enrichment=partial, continue else Healthy G-->>F: {zone_id, entered: true} end F->>T: Batched upsert (5k rows) F->>K: produce → shipment.events K->>S: consume shipment.events S->>S: Apply state machine transition S->>K: produce → shipment.status_changed K->>N: consume status_changed N->>C: POST webhook (HMAC-signed) alt Webhook 5xx or timeout C--xN: failure N->>N: Exponential backoff, max 6 retries N->>K: produce → webhook.dlq (after exhaustion) else Success C-->>N: 200 OK end end ``` ### 4.1 Latency Budget The p95 end-to-end budget of **800ms** decomposes as: | Segment | Budget | Observed p95 | Headroom | |---------|--------|--------------|----------| | Device → Edge | 180ms | 142ms | 38ms | | Edge → Kafka produce | 25ms | 18ms | 7ms | | Kafka → Flink consume | 120ms | 96ms | 24ms | | Dedupe + enrich | 200ms | 231ms | **−31ms** ⚠️ | | Timescale upsert | 150ms | 119ms | 31ms | | Queryable visibility | 125ms | 88ms | 37ms | | **Total** | **800ms** | **694ms** | 106ms | ⚠️ The enrichment stage is over budget. The `GeofenceJoin` async I/O timeout is the dominant contributor during PostGIS autovacuum windows. Tracked as **HEL-4412**. --- ## 5. Tenant Isolation Model Helios uses a **hybrid isolation** approach — shared compute, partitioned storage. ### 5.1 Isolation Boundaries ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Shared: Edge Gateway, Flink cluster, Kafka brokers │ │ Isolation via: rate limits, partition keys, quotas │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Partitioned: TimescaleDB hypertables, PG row-level │ │ Isolation via: RLS policies + tenant_id partition key │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Dedicated: Enterprise tier optimizer pods, S3 prefixes │ │ Isolation via: namespace, IAM boundary, node taints │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### 5.2 Row-Level Security Every tenant-scoped table enforces RLS. Application connections assume a role with no `BYPASSRLS`: ```sql CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON shipments USING (tenant_id = current_setting('helios.tenant_id')::uuid); ALTER TABLE shipments ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ALTER TABLE shipments FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; ``` The connection pool sets `helios.tenant_id` in a transaction-local `SET LOCAL` before checkout. A middleware assertion fails the request if the setting is unset — this has caught **4** isolation bugs in staging since introduction. ### 5.3 Noisy Neighbor Controls | Control | Mechanism | Trigger | |---------|-----------|---------| | Ingest throttle | Token bucket at edge | Sustained >120% of tier limit | | Query concurrency cap | PG `pg_bouncer` per-tenant pool | >8 concurrent analytical queries | | Optimizer preemption | K8s PriorityClass | Enterprise job queued >30s | | Circuit break | Per-tenant Hystrix bulkhead | Error rate >25% over 60s | --- ## 6. Failure Modes and Mitigations ### 6.1 Degradation Ladder Helios degrades in a defined order. Each level sheds capability to protect the level below it. | Level | Trigger | Shed | Preserved | |-------|---------|------|-----------| | L0 | Normal | — | All | | L1 | Ingest lag >60s | ETA re-prediction | Position tracking, webhooks | | L2 | Ingest lag >300s | Geofence enrichment | Raw position writes | | L3 | TimescaleDB write failure | All writes → Kafka buffer | Read path from cache | | L4 | Multi-AZ loss | Write path fully offline | Read-only tracking API | ### 6.2 Known Weaknesses 1. **Kafka buffer depth at L3 is finite.** At 240k events/sec and 7-day retention sizing, we have roughly **4.5 hours** before the buffer saturates. Runbook `RB-0031` covers emergency topic expansion, but it requires manual broker provisioning. 2. **`tenant-svc` is a hard dependency of the edge.** Its 99.99% SLO is aspirational — measured trailing-90-day availability is **99.973%**. A `tenant-svc` outage fails the entire ingest path closed. The 60s resolution cache softens this but does not eliminate it. 3. **Webhook DLQ has no automated replay.** Exhausted webhooks land in `webhook.dlq` and require an operator to run the replay tool. During the March incident this produced a 31-hour notification gap for 12 tenants. --- ## 7. It runs as a fleet of stateless Envoy-fronted Go services across three regions. **Responsibilities:** 1. TLS termination and mTLS validation for telematics devices 2. Tenant resolution from API key, JWT claim, or device certificate SAN 3. Rate limiting (token bucket, per-tenant, backed by Redis) 4.
